title: Choose the Analytics workspace
question: Each option keeps ASC Studio’s calm operator interface, shows metric provenance and freshness, and turns Apple data into decisions. Choose the structure that should organize analysis.

options.label: Analysis Notebook
options.lineage: Saved Appfigures-style reports with a persistent evidence canvas
options.thesis: Start from a concise performance pulse, then keep each investigation as a reusable view with its filters, comparison, and findings intact.
options.viewport: A slim saved-view rail and global date controls frame one large comparison chart, pinned KPIs, contribution breakdowns, and a cited What changed note.
options.risk: Saved reports must remain lightweight so the workspace feels like analysis, not a document manager.

options.label: Portfolio Pulse
options.lineage: Adaptive portfolio overview with app-level drill-down
options.thesis: Show every app’s material movement first, then expand the selected app into acquisition, engagement, revenue, and quality evidence.
options.viewport: A compact app roster ranks meaningful changes on the left while the selected app owns a broad trend canvas and ranked driver table on the right.
options.risk: The portfolio view is less useful for a single-app operator unless the selected-app analysis remains dominant.

options.label: What Changed Workbench
options.thesis: Organize the workspace around the questions operators actually ask: what changed, where, why might it have changed, and what should I inspect next?
options.viewport: A question switcher and global filters lead into one dominant trend, a ranked drivers panel, and evidence-linked actions into Storefront, Releases, Reviews, or Apple Ads.
options.risk: The guidance must label correlation as a hypothesis and never let AI imply causation from thin data.
